typesafe: unavailable, unchanged from the previous round and re-checked rather than retried blindly. argv: `test -n "$TYPESAFE_API_KEY"` in the same shell the client would run in; the key is absent, which is the exact condition that returned exit 3 last round with `typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment ...)`. No Jev judgment was consumed in this round either; every judgment below is reviewer_reason formed locally from the named evidence, and no producer-owned Jev result was reused.

F2 resolution, read at 6cd6d33 against the remedy I named. The bound is now a check that trips, at the place that owns the setting: crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/config.rs:47 declares `pub const MAX_RELOAD_MS: u64 = 20_000` as the one owner of the number, and IntegrationSettings::from_lookup (config.rs:260) reads the value and returns `ConfigError::ReloadTooSlow { value }` before constructing any Self, so no settings value above the bound is ever produced - the refusal is decided on a pure read before anything serves. crates/foundry-app/src/main.rs:346-359 turns that Err into `event = "health.startup.refused", probe = "integrations", detail = %err` and `return Err(err.into())`, so the server refuses to start; the interpolated value is a u64, never a secret. The refusal says WHAT, WHY and HOW in one sentence: it names FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS, the value read, the 20000 ms (20 s) bound, why the gate needs it (a server polling that slowly leaves longer between two of its own beats than another counts one as current for, so running servers look gone to one another and an admin is offered a way out that discards credentials they are still serving with), and two remedies (unset it for the 5000 ms default, or set it to 20000 or less). The duplication my finding would otherwise have created is closed rather than added: LiveOpeners::RELOAD_ENVELOPE at secrets_key_rotation.rs:144 is now `time::Duration::milliseconds(MAX_RELOAD_MS as i64)`, so the bound and the window it sizes are one fact and WINDOW stays exactly 40 s, which the unchanged independent LAW_WINDOW literal in the T3 and T4 checks would catch if it moved. The withdrawn claim is withdrawn in writing: ADR-IIS-SKR-004 Decision states "The backstop claim is withdrawn: I-28a covers only the server of an earlier release that beats no row at all, which is what its words say", so the I-28a copy at handlers/secrets_key.rs:97 is no longer asked to carry a hazard it does not name. The operator documentation agrees with the code on both sides: RELEASING.md:382 states the admitted 1 to 20000 range, the breaking change and "Lower it before upgrading", and docs/product/architecture/brief.md:1144 and :1220 state the same range and keep the acceptance 200 ms inside it. I verified no deployment, harness or probe asks for more than the bound: every setter of FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS in the repository is the acceptance support's 200 ms constant or the probe's 200. F2 is resolved and I removed it.

F1 resolution, read at 6cd6d33. The stale sentence is no longer live authority: docs/product/architecture/ADR-IIS-SKR-003.md now reads `Status: Superseded by IIS-SKR-004` (changed in this delta), and the superseding Accepted ADR names the error and corrects the record. ADR-IIS-SKR-004 Context: "Its Consequences say the gate window model is unchecked, which the receipt beside the model contradicts: it was replayed in the shared Lima VM local-dev." ADR-IIS-SKR-004 Consequences: "The model is checked, not unchecked: in local-dev with quint 0.32.0 and openjdk 21.0.12.1, both invariants NoError under quint verify at bound 44, the tightness witness refuted and mutants m8 and m9 killed, recorded command by command with its exit status in docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/design/live_replica_gate.receipt.txt." That is the claim the receipt supports, at the strength the receipt gives, with the path a reader can rerun. architecture.md already stated it correctly. Correcting the record in the superseding decision rather than rewriting the body of a superseded one is the right shape: a superseded ADR keeps the text it was decided with. The obligation I cited - the document set agrees with the evidence the same change carries, and the wrong side is fixed in that change - now holds, so F1 is resolved and I removed it. The only place the refuted sentence survives is inside a Superseded ADR, as history.

Oracle completeness and non-circularity for L14, the one new law in this delta. crates/foundry-app/tests/iis_secrets_key_bound.rs drives the public door the design named, IntegrationSettings::from_lookup, through a lookup of its own that answers only FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS, and covers every case the acceptance row declares: nothing set reads as the 5000 ms default; "abc", "1.5", "-1" and "20 s" are refused as ConfigError::NotANumber for that setting and explicitly not as out of range; 0 and 1 are admitted and read as 1 ms; the generated range 1..=20000 and the 20000 boundary are admitted and read as given; 20001, 60000, u64::MAX and the generated range 20001..=u64::MAX are refused with no settings value produced; and each refusal must name the setting, the exact value read and the bound. ENVELOPE_MS is an independent literal 20_000 written in the test and never read from MAX_RELOAD_MS, which is what the acceptance row requires ("worked out from the bound itself, not from what the read answers") and what keeps the check non-circular - raising MAX_RELOAD_MS alone would turn this test red. Every assertion is behavioural on the public read's outcome; none is tautological, none mocks the subject, and each failure message names the user-visible consequence. The row's own declared gap is that the test pins the refusal's three facts but not the surrounding operator prose, and leaves that to review: I checked it, and RELEASING.md:382 and brief.md:1144 state the same 1-to-20000 range as MAX_RELOAD_MS and the refusal message. Nothing was weakened anywhere in the delta: no scenario, assertion or input range was removed, narrowed or softened, no test was skipped or ignored, and the only change to an existing test is the T3 proptest gaining `failure_persistence: None` with `cases` still 256 - that stops proptest writing a regression file into the source tree and changes neither the generators nor the assertions. The new test keeps the dominant repository setting (plain with_cases(256)), so the two differ in that one field; I judge that a consistency nit with no effect on discrimination and raise no finding on it.

diagnostic:
Accepted, with no finding open. Both design findings of the previous round are resolved by this delta and removed; the reassessment covers 06fabde..6cd6d33 only and retains every judgment of the accepted record at 4ec4231, whose inputs this delta does not touch.

F2, the unbounded reload envelope, is resolved at the place that owns the setting rather than papered over. MAX_RELOAD_MS = 20_000 at config.rs:47 is now the one owner of the number; IntegrationSettings::from_lookup refuses ConfigError::ReloadTooSlow before it constructs any settings value, so no server ever serves above the bound, and main.rs:346 turns that into health.startup.refused and a refusal to start. The refusal says WHAT, WHY and HOW in one sentence and names the value it read, which is a u64 and no secret. The fix removes duplication instead of adding it: LiveOpeners::RELOAD_ENVELOPE now reads MAX_RELOAD_MS, so the bound and the 40 s window it sizes are one fact, and the independent LAW_WINDOW literal of T3 and T4 would catch the window moving. The claim my finding said the shipped I-28a copy could not carry is withdrawn in writing in ADR-IIS-SKR-004's Decision, and both operator documents, RELEASING.md and the product brief, now state the admitted range and the breaking change. I checked that no deployment, harness or probe in the repository asks for more than the bound.

F1, the stale Consequences sentence, is resolved the right way round: ADR-IIS-SKR-003 is now Superseded by IIS-SKR-004, and ADR-IIS-SKR-004 names the contradiction in its Context and records the checked claim with the receipt path in its Consequences. A superseded decision keeps the text it was decided with, so correcting the record in the superseding ADR is better than rewriting the old body, which is what my remediation had asked for.

The new law L14 has an executable oracle, not production support mistaken for coverage. crates/foundry-app/tests/iis_secrets_key_bound.rs drives the public door the design named and covers the whole text a deployment can leave in the setting: unset reads as the default, non-numeric stays its own error rather than an out-of-range one, 0 and 1 read as 1 ms, the generated range up to the 20000 boundary is admitted and read as given, everything above it is refused with no settings value produced, and each refusal must name the setting, the exact value and the bound. Its ENVELOPE_MS is an independent literal, never read from MAX_RELOAD_MS, so raising the bound alone turns the test red - the check cannot go green by agreeing with the code. I verified the operator prose the test deliberately does not pin, and RELEASING.md and brief.md agree with both the constant and the refusal.

Nothing was weakened. No scenario, assertion or input range was removed, narrowed or softened; no test is skipped or ignored; the smoke exception the RED commit carried is gone from xtask and the new test file carries no #[ignore]; the only change to an existing test is the T3 proptest gaining failure_persistence: None with cases still 256, which stops a regression file being written into the source tree and touches neither generators nor assertions.

Evidence: I reused the host's complete native smoke at exit 0 on a byte-identical tree - 95 suites ok, no failure, the one ignored item a pre-existing foundry-realtime doc-test - in which the new oracle test ran and passed by name, and I executed the one check smoke excludes. The us-iis-07 lane at this commit returned exit 0 with 32 scenarios (32 passed) and 571 steps (571 passed) on its first run, so the producer's 32/32 is now observed. Nothing required is unrun or stale.

Limits retained: Jev is still unavailable, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this environment, so every judgment here is reviewer_reason formed locally and no producer Jev result was reused; the project ships no test-impact selector, so selection was mechanical from the touched paths; I measured no test timings, there being no budget statement or derogation in scope.
